# Panic on invalid parseArgs data

## Pull Request by @tomusdrw

## Summary
- `parseArgs` in `RefineContext` and `AccumulateContext` now panics on invalid data instead of returning `Result<T, ParseError>`
- Removed the `ParseError` enum — no longer needed
- Simplified all callsites (SDK tests + 3 examples) from 5-line Result checks to single assignments
- Added "Panic on invalid host data" guideline to `CODING_GUIDELINES.md`

Entry point arguments are host-provided — if they're malformed, recovery is meaningless. This is consistent with how fetchers already handle host-contract violations (panic, not Result).

## Test plan
- [x] All 129 tests pass (`npm test` — SDK 91 + ecalli-test 31 + all-ecalli 2 + fibonacci 5)
- [x] Biome formatting/linting passes

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Walkthrough

This PR changes AccumulateContext.parseArgs and RefineContext.parseArgs to return parsed argument structs directly instead of Result<…, ParseError>. Parsing failures (decode errors, trailing bytes, or malformed host entry-point args) now call panic(...) rather than returning a Result error. The exported ParseError enum was removed. Documentation, examples, and tests were updated to stop handling parse errors via Result and to use ctx.parseArgs / ctx.yieldHash-style APIs that assume host-provided data is either valid or a panic-inducing contract violation.

- tomusdrw/as-lan#79: Converts Result/error-based parsing and fetch APIs to panic/optional semantics, addressing the same error-handling design and SDK parsing/fetch code.

</details>
